summary: Second retest of the HIGH mirror 2-shot stitch bias. I used the iteration_23 camera mock: canvas.captureStream 960x1000, upper.jpg then lower.jpg drawn contain-fit, mirror mode, two snaps, as user_avatar_test at 168 cm / 60 kg. RESULT: STILL FAILING. registerParts() returns s=0.9057, t=538.3, dx=41.5. I captured these from the real drawImage(l.bitmap, dx, t, l.W*s, l.H*s) call, and an in-page replica of the pose.js math gives the same numbers. Ground truth is s=1.0, t=576-577, dx=0. Stitched measurements: chest 83 / waist 72 / hips 96 / shoulder 38 / inseam 78. Single-shot fullbody.jpg re-run today at the same height: 76 / 65 / 89 / 33 / 80. Errors: chest +9.2%, waist +10.8%, hips +7.9%, shoulder +15%, inseam -2.5%. Analysis is fast: the avatar POST fires about 1.1s after the second snap and avatar-ready shows at 1.9s (target < 5s), so PASS. ui_bugs.issue: The registration picks the wrong minimum, s=0.906 / t=538 instead of s=1.0 / t=577, because the cost is not robust to the mask taper at the bottom edge of photo 1. Profile 'a' runs to u.H-3, and its last ~7 rows have collapsing widths (y943..949: 235, 231, 176, 102, 60, 27, 16). The per-row error |a.w - s*b.w| / a.w explodes there: at y=948 it is |27-262|/27 = 8.7. These few rows dominate the mean. At ground truth the other rows match within 1-4px (e.g. y818 a=218 b=218, y878 231/231, y938 257/256). Even so, the GT cost is 0.1425 against 0.1266 for the wrong solution, because the wrong s maps the bottom rows onto narrow leg rows of photo 2.

The requested hint text change is not in the code. It still says 'dalla testa ai fianchi' / 'dai fianchi ai piedi (i fianchi sulla linea dorata)'. It should be 'dalla testa a metà coscia…' / 'dalla vita ai piedi…'. The silhouette gold lines also still guide the user to put the hips on the line.

issues: The seam is visible with the current s/t/dx: mean abs grey diff across seam rows y845/848 is 6.4, against 1.2 on control rows. If I rebuild the stitch with s=1, t=577, dx=0, the seam diff is 1.2, i.e. invisible.

action_items: HIGH pose.js registerParts: make the cost robust. These are verified in an in-page replica on the same MediaPipe masks. Per-row error clamped with Math.min(err, 0.15) → s=1.000, t=577 (cost 0.033). Median instead of mean → s=1.000, t=577. Symmetric normalisation |a-sb| / max(a, sb) → s=1.000, t=575. Trimming only y < u.H-15 does NOT help, because the taper is at u.bottom (949), not at u.H. If you trim, trim relative to u.bottom (e.g. drop rows y > u.bottom - 0.02*u.H) AND clamp. Recommended: clamp at 0.15 + exclude rows within 2% of u.bottom.

HIGH pose.js inseam/legLen: with fixed registration, legLen = feetY - u.hipY gives inseam_r 0.508 against single-shot 0.480 (+5.8%). u.hipY in photo 1 sits 28.6 fullbody-px too HIGH (660.7 vs 689.3 in single-shot), which is landmark drift near the frame edge. The photo-2 hip mapped into photo 1 (t + s*l.hipY = 911 → 714.5 fb-px) sits 25 px too LOW. Their average (≈687.6) is within 2 px of the truth. Using hipRef = (u.hipY + t + s*l.hipY)/2 for legLen gives inseam_r ≈ 0.482 (+0.4%).

Expected ratios after the registration fix (fixed vs single-shot): shoulder 0.1621 vs 0.1695 (-4.4%), chest 0.1621 vs 0.1695 (-4.4%), waist 0.1426 vs 0.1491 (-4.4%), hips 0.1837 vs 0.1946 (-5.6%). bodyH matches within 0.5% (882.5 vs 878.4 fullbody px), so the remaining ~4-5% comes from landmark/mask differences between photos, not from the stitch.

critical_code_review_comments: registerParts: the 0.15/sqrt(n) overlap prior is fine. The problem is only the unbounded relative error on near-zero widths. Also consider skipping rows where a.w < 0.5 * median(a.w).
registerParts: the dx median is affected by the same wrong s/t (dx=41.5px, truth 0). It will self-correct once s/t are right.
chest is always capped at the shoulder width (chest_r == shoulder_r in both single-shot and 2-shot). This is pre-existing; consider whether the cap is too tight.

rca of the issue: Root cause: profile 'a' in photo 1 includes the bottom ~7 rows, where the segmentation mask tapers to almost zero width (the body is cut by the frame bottom). The relative error divides by a.w, so these rows produce errors of 1-9, while correct rows produce ~0.01. The mean cost is minimised by shrinking s, so that those rows land on narrow regions of photo 2, which trades a good match everywhere else for less outlier error. Repro: run /tmp/harness.js on the app origin; found s=0.9057 t=538 (cost 0.1266), GT s=1 t=576 (cost 0.1425). Mitigation: clamp the per-row error (or use the median) and drop rows near u.bottom. All three robust variants give s=1.000, t=575-577.
